outcome: Experiment Authoring now owns rendered syntax colors instead of relying on incidental Ace theme styling
owner_impact: The Search field/button remains as previously verified. The macOS highlighting repair now works at the visual rendering layer: Virtual Lab defines its own scoped colors for keywords, strings, comments, numbers, language constants, functions, parameters and invalid syntax, so tokenized code cannot silently render as one monochrome color because an Ace theme failed to load or apply.

next.text: The reopened #513 scope is complete after the rendered-color repair. The owner should refresh the live Lab on macOS and verify the visual highlighting; no successor ticket is implied by this repair.

technical_evidence: Root cause: the prior implementation verified Ace Python tokenization but Virtual Lab CSS set one base editor text color and supplied no deterministic token-color palette.
Virtual Lab now owns the visible Ace token palette in react-chrome.css, scoped to the authoring editor and independent of Ace theme-module loading or browser/CDN timing.
The existing deterministic Python-mode preload/reassertion remains in place.

Production smoke still switches Configuration, Initialization, Controller and Metrics twice, but now also reads computed DOM colors for rendered token spans and requires at least one visible token color distinct from the editor base color for every artifact on every pass.
Search remains covered separately and is not changed by this repair.
